instruction.text: Use the information to fill in the gaps.

atoms.a: On day 1, Jackson has 10 baguettes in his pantry. Each day afterwards, he eats 2 baguettes.
atoms.b: To get to the next term, ((++subtract add)) <mat><gap>1 ++2 3</gap></mat>.
After the third day, he will have <mat><gap>6</gap></mat> baguettes left.
Jackson will run out of baguettes on day <mat><gap>6</gap></mat>.

instruction.text: Use the information to fill in the gaps.

atoms.a: Natsuki is saving up for a trip. At the end of the first month he has saved up £150. At the end of the third month he has saved up £450.
atoms.b: To get to the next term, ((subtract ++add)) <mat><gap>++150 200 300</gap></mat>.
At the end of the fourth month, he will have saved up £<mat><gap>600</gap></mat>.

atoms.a: His trip will cost him £1,000. For how long does he have to save up?
atoms.b: Natsuki will have £1,000 by the end of month <mat><gap>7</gap></mat>.

instruction.text: Use the information to fill in the gaps.

atoms.a: Emma’s monthly rent is going up by £100 each year. In the first year, rent costs £550 each month.
atoms.b: To get to the next term, ((subtract ++add)) <mat><gap>550 ++100 650</gap></mat>.

atoms.a: If Emma makes £1,000 per month, when will she no longer be able to afford her rent?
atoms.sound: If Emma makes 1,000 pounds per month, when will she no longer be able to afford her rent?
atoms.b: Emma won’t be able to afford rent in the <mat><gap>6</gap></mat>th year.
